On the final day of South Carolina's GOP Senate runoff, MAGA Inc deployed nearly $830k to support Darline Graham against rival candidate Ralph Norman.

The Poison:
Withholding major PAC funds until the final day prevents voters and opponents from engaging with or scrutinizing the influx of outside influence.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing personal loyalty to an endorsement (WHO) with transparent policy debate (WHAT). A classic bait-and-switch where brand cachet replaces local merit.

Social Physics Analysis:
Instead of fostering open dialogue across South Carolina counties, late super PAC money relies on broadcast saturation and phone blasts to manufacture momentum.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. (-0.8 * 0.8)

The Unavoidable Truth: Late financial infusions heavily sway compressed primary runoffs.

The Unavoidable Lie: Super PAC spending is purely a grassroots expression of voter will.

Alethekanon:
Late financial saturation bypasses local deliberation, substituting external branding for genuine constituent engagement. The super PAC apparatus replaces dialogue with volume.

Awwthekanon:
Elections should be about listening to local communities, not last-minute cash avalanches. When big money drops on the eve of a vote, everyday voices get drowned out.

Brothekanon:
Dropping nearly $830k on the literal final day of the race is the political equivalent of a buzzer-beater 3-pointer. Subtle it is definitely not.
